chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abd al-Karim from Abi Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Tamattu' (Hajj) but could not afford the sacrificial animal (Hady) until the Day of Departure (Yawm al-Nafar) when he found the price of a sheep. I asked: Should he slaughter or fast? He said: 'Rather, he should fast, for the days of slaughter have passed.'

Thus, there is no contradiction in it with what we said, because the meaning of this report is for the one who fasted three days and then found the price of the Hady; upon him is to fast for the remainder to complete ten days, and the Hady is not obligatory upon him. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَيَّامَ الذَّبْحِ: The days of slaughter (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّفْرِ: The Day of Departure (after standing at Arafat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who finds money for the Hajj sacrifice after the days of slaughter have passed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who acquires the means for the Hady after the days of Tashriq have passed, the obligation shifts entirely to completing the ten-day fast rather than offering the sacrifice. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the timing of the Hady is strictly tied to the days of Eid al-Adha, and missing this window exempts the pilgrim from the animal sacrifice while maintaining the validity of the compensatory fasting.
